column1: # Lines tools/defercheck reports that are not deferred work, with the reason
# each one is allowed to stay.
# FOUR tab separated fields: the tracked path, the RULE the row excuses, a
# literal FRAGMENT of the line it excuses, and why that line is not a deferral.
# THE FRAGMENT IS THE POINT OF THIS FILE and it is what makes it different from
# a list of directories to ignore. A row that named only a path would excuse
# that file forever, so the row below for .github/workflows/ci.yml, which
# describes a marker in another project's parser, would silently cover the next
# marker somebody writes anywhere in that 900 line workflow. A row has to quote
# a piece of the line it excuses, so it covers that line and nothing else.
# A FRAGMENT MUST NOT CONTAIN THE PHRASE ITS RULE MATCHES. This file is tracked,
# so the gate reads it like any other, and a row quoting the marker it excuses
# is itself a hit. Two rows did exactly that the first time this file was
# committed, and the gate refused them. Quote a neighbouring piece of the line.
# A row that matches nothing FAILS the gate. An exemption that excuses nothing
# is a claim about the tree that stopped being true, and left alone it becomes a
# licence nobody granted.
# There are four reasons here and they are genuinely four different things.
# None of them is "this file is allowed to be unfinished".
#   A QUOTATION. Three rows quote another project's own words: dependabot-core's
#   parser, Docker's deprecation notice for the legacy builder, and Astro's
#   warning about a route collision. Each is a sentence about somebody else's
#   software, and each is load bearing where it stands, because it is the
#   evidence for a decision this repository made.
#   A FORMAT PLACEHOLDER. One row is the shape of an error code, three capital
#   letters between a prefix and a number, written in a comment that explains
#   how a code is recognised. The letters are the format rather than a slot
#   nobody filled.
#   A SIBLING GATE'S OWN RULE. tools/docs/forbidden.sh refuses these markers in
#   documentation, so its rule list and its tests have to contain them. A
#   checker cannot be exempted from itself, which is why this tool assembles its
#   own marker words from fragments rather than appearing here.
#   A FIXTURE. tools/extdoc's test writes a page that says the product is about
#   to do something, because refusing that page is what the test is for.
# path
.github/workflows/ci.yml
